title: Adversarial replay of the integrity guards
description: Attack T-417/T-418 the way the verifiers attacked T-407/T-410: try to get a clerk ballot in under an aliased name, a backdated conclude, a discussion round that is an empty string. Verdict done or send back with reproduction.

notes.note:
REJECTED: real, blocking escape in T-418 guard 1 (discussion evidence). Sending T-418 back.

MANDATE: attack idea explicitly listed in T-419: "conclude after deleting the alternatives
list." Ran it. It works.

MECHANISM: undiscussed_alternatives() re-validates at conclude by iterating
dossier.get("alternatives", []) and returning [a for a in alternatives if a not in
discussed]. If the dossier's "alternatives" array is hand-edited to [] (or the key deleted
entirely) AFTER voting but BEFORE conclude, that list comprehension is vacuously empty --
"no alternatives" reads as "nothing left to discuss," not "everything is undiscussed."
undiscussed_alternatives() returns [], conclude's `if missing:` guard never fires, and
conclude SUCCEEDS with a Condorcet tally on the surviving final_ballots even though ZERO
discuss calls were ever made. The tally itself is computed straight from final_ballots and
never reads "alternatives" at all, so the emptied/deleted field costs the attacker nothing
downstream.

This is squarely in-scope of the guard's own declared threat model: the guard's docstring and
the existing test test_hand_edited_empty_round_does_not_satisfy_the_guard already assume and
defend against a hand-edited dossier ("a hand-edited empty entry does not count"). It defends
the discussion ROUNDS against hand-editing but never the alternatives LIST the rounds are
checked against -- same json file, same attacker capability, undefended.

REPRO 1 (empty list), own execution, scratch harness-root only, live .harness/deliberations
and .harness/roster.json untouched throughout (confirmed via git status --short before/after
-- no diff outside my own scratch dirs):

  SCRATCH=<scratch>/attack1 ; cp .harness/roster.json "$SCRATCH/roster.json"
  deliberate.py propose --title escape-test --evidence T-419 --task T-419 --proposer
    registro-a --alternatives adopt --alternatives reject --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py sponsor D-001 --by registro-b --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py sponsor D-001 --by revision-doctrina --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py prior D-001 --voter registro-a --ranking adopt,reject --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py prior D-001 --voter registro-b --ranking reject,adopt --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py schedule D-001 --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py vote D-001 --voter registro-a --ranking adopt,reject --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  deliberate.py vote D-001 --voter registro-b --ranking reject,adopt --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  # BEFORE edit: conclude correctly refuses --
  #   "refused: no discussion recorded for alternative(s) 'adopt', 'reject' ..." exit 1
  python3 -c "import json,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('$SCRATCH/deliberations/D-001.json');
    d=json.loads(p.read_text()); d['alternatives']=[]; p.write_text(json.dumps(d))"
  deliberate.py conclude D-001 --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  # => "DELIBERATION CONCLUDED: D-001 ... Winner: adopt ... Deliberation:
  #     NO-DELIBERATION-OBSERVED", EXIT 0. Zero discuss calls ever made on this dossier.

REPRO 2 (key deletion instead of empty list, and non-unanimous ballots so the unanimity flag
is not confounding the read -- final ballots deliberately DIFFER from priors this time): same
lifecycle, then
  python3 -c "import json,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('$SCRATCH/deliberations/D-001.json');
    d=json.loads(p.read_text()); del d['alternatives']; p.write_text(json.dumps(d))"
  deliberate.py conclude D-001 --harness-root "$SCRATCH"
  # => "Winner: adopt ... Deliberation: deliberation-observed", EXIT 0. Confirms this is an
  #    isolated Guard-1 defeat: Guard 2 (unanimity flag) read correctly in this run
  #    (ballots differed from priors, flag correctly did NOT fire) while Guard 1 was fully
  #    bypassed in the same conclude call.

COVERAGE CHECK: grep -n "alternatives" .harness/tests/test_deliberate.py shows every existing
test only ever SETS alternatives at propose time or hand-edits "discussion" entries
(test_hand_edited_empty_round_does_not_satisfy_the_guard). No test hand-edits or deletes the
"alternatives" field itself. This is a genuine gap, not a duplicate of covered ground.

4 OTHER ATTACK VECTORS RUN, ALL HELD (no new escape, listed for completeness / cognitive
diversity beyond the producer's own regression classes):
1. Alternative renamed in the dossier's alternatives list AFTER its discussion round was
   recorded (discuss re="reject" recorded, then alternatives list rewritten to
   ["adopt","rejected"]) -> conclude correctly refuses: "no discussion recorded for
   alternative(s) 'rejected'", exit 1. Fails closed, no bypass.
2. Timestamp skew boundary re-tested in a NEW nesting shape (list-of-lists-of-dicts,
   different from the producer's own test fixtures): stamp at exactly now+300s inside
   weird_nested[0][0]["inner"][0]["deep_stamp"] -> allowed, exit 0 (boundary is ">", not
   ">="); now+301s in the same shape -> refused, exit 1; a syntactically ISO-shaped but
   calendar-invalid string ("2026-13-45T99:99:99Z") in the same nested position -> refused
   (unparseable fails closed), exit 1; `show` on a future-dated dossier -> exit 0 (reads stay
   open). All matches documented behavior.
3. Unicode-lookalike clerk name (Cyrillic 'е' substituted for Latin 'e' in "fed-relator") ->
   refused as unissued name (exact dict-key match, no homoglyph privilege), exit 1.
4. colegiado value forced to a bare list (non-dict) -> clean "roster inconsistent: ... is not
   an object" refusal, exit 1, no traceback. A colegiado retrofitted with clerk markers in its
   charter text under a NON-fedatario name ("registro" + "NO legisla, NO vota") correctly
   refuses registro-a as a clerk seat too -- confirms charter-driven, not name-driven,
   detection as designed.

  pytest .harness/tests -q -> 816 passed, 4 skipped (matches hand-off).
Suite passing does not contradict the finding: no test exercises this path.

HOUSEKEEPING: lock.py status -> "no active lock files"; lock.py sweep -> "swept 0 expired

FIX NEEDED (for the T-418 owner, not prescribing implementation but naming the shape of the
gap): undiscussed_alternatives() must not treat an empty/absent "alternatives" list as
"nothing to discuss." Either re-validate against alternatives captured immutably at propose
time (never trust dossier["alternatives"] at conclude for what MUST be checked), or refuse
conclude outright when "alternatives" is empty/missing on a dossier that has final_ballots
recorded (a concluded dossier with no alternatives at all is itself a red flag). Needs its own
regression test alongside the existing hand-edited-discussion-round class.

CLOSED: fulfilled by T-418 round-2 verification (same agent, same session). T-419's mandate --
adversarially replay the T-417/T-418 integrity guards and verdict done or send back with
reproduction -- is exactly what was executed while verifying T-418's round-2 fix for the
escape T-419 (verifier-t419) found in round 1 (alternatives=[] / key-deletion bypassing the
discussion-evidence guard).

Round-2 replay re-ran T-419's own two repro variants (empty-list, key-deletion) plus 4 net-new
attack vectors on the fixed effective_alternatives() mechanism (malformed empty-everything
case, prior-only undiscussed candidate, whitespace-only hand-edited discussion round,
post-discuss ballot injection of an undiscussed candidate, case-sensitive alternative variant,
write-in-candidate no-deadlock path) plus full regression re-check of T-417's clerk gate and
T-418 guards 2/3 (unanimity flag + future-stamp incl. dict keys). All held; no further escape.
One non-blocking robustness finding (uncaught crash, not a bypass, on a non-dict final_ballots
value under raw JSON tampering) noted for future hardening, not blocking.
